title: Cache-aware token regen scratchpad
content:
Purpose
----
Quick personal scratchpad to explore a pricing/credits idea that accounts for request-level cache hit behavior (prefix/KV reuse) rather than purely per-output token pricing. The goal is a small, implementable billing primitive that: (a) credits customers when cache substantially reduces compute, (b) preserves simple mental model for customers, and (c) maps cleanly to our runtime metrics (gpu-ms / token / cache-hit-rate).

High-level idea
----
Instead of only charging per-output-token, charge two components: 1) baseline (session/req) + 2) compute units tied to "regenerated tokens" where regeneration means tokens that required model attention because KV/prefix cache did not supply them. If the runtime can report an approximation of regenerated tokens (or convert GPU time to token-equivalent), we can credit customers on cache hits.

Key assumptions / metrics we can access
----
- avg_gpu_ms_per_token (baseline for new tokens) ~ 0.12 ms/token (in a typical 8k Llama-like model on our optimized runtime)  -- placeholder, needs real telemetry
- avg_prefix_reuse: fraction of tokens served from cache (0.0 - 0.9)
- observed_cache_hit_rate = #requests with partial/full KV hit / total requests
- p99_sequence_length and mean_output_tokens
- ability to emit a per-request metric: regenerated_tokens_estimate OR measured_gpu_ms
- cost per GPU-ms (amortized) -> internal reference (use $0.00012 / gpu-ms for calc below as back-of-envelope)

Notation and simple formula
----
Let:
R = requested output tokens (user-visible tokens)
H = fraction of R served from cache (0..1). H=0 means no cache benefit.
G = avg_gpu_ms_per_regen_token
C_gpu = $ cost per gpu-ms
Then: regenerated_tokens = R * (1 - H)
Compute_cost_per_req = regenerated_tokens * G * C_gpu
If we bill tokens directly, we can define an "effective billable tokens" = regenerated_tokens + alpha * R (alpha is tiny baseline fraction to cover routing/IO)

Numeric examples (toy)
----
Example parameters (toy): R=200 tokens per request, H=0.6 (60% cache reuse), G=0.12 ms/token, C_gpu = $0.00012 / gpu-ms
regenerated_tokens = 200 * (1-0.6) = 80 tokens
gpu_ms_for_regen = 80 * 0.12 = 9.6 ms
compute_cost = 9.6 * 0.00012 = $0.001152 per request (~$1.15 per 1k requests)
If we billed naive per-token at $0.0002 / token (example), naive_cost = 200 * 0.0002 = $0.04 per req. Big difference => per-token would overcharge when cache works.

What to expose to customers
----
Option A (simple): present "regenerated tokens" as billable tokens on invoice. Show cache-hit % and a line item: regen tokens = X, baseline small fixed per-request fee. This is transparent but requires careful naming ("regenerated tokens" is internal jargon).
Option B (banded tiers): define bands for cache-hit buckets, e.g., 0-20% (full price), 20-60% (partial discount), >60% (high reuse discount). Easier to explain but less precise.
Option C (hybrid): bill a small per-call connection fee + per-regenerated-token price. Show both on console, keep invoice simple.

Tier examples (back-of-envelope)
----
Assume we want 3 simple SKUs for hosted API:
- Starter: per-regened-token $0.00022 + $0.0005 per request baseline
- Scale: per-regened-token $0.00016 + $0.00025 per request baseline; committed discounts on regened tokens for reserved customers
- Enterprise: per-regened-token $0.00012 + $0.0x per request baseline; dedicated dedicated pool pricing negotiated

Plugging toy numbers from above: for R=200, H=0.6 => regen=80; Starter cost = 80*0.00022 + 0.0005 = $0.0181 (~$18 per 1k req). Versus naive per-token we'd charge 200 * 0.00022 = $0.044 => cache-aware reduces cost for customer.

Edge cases and complications
----
- Warm vs cold KV: first request that populates KV should not get a credit; we need to track whether cache result is from warm state or cold fill. Could mark those requests as not eligible for cache credit.
- Long tails: very long outputs will still be expensive; ensure we handle spikes and p99 correctly (maybe cap per-request credits to avoid gaming).
- Privacy/regulatory: private deployments with no shared cache should still benefit from local cache; billing must respect customer isolation.
- Accuracy vs simplicity: measuring GPU-ms precisely is ideal but may be noisy and harder as an invoice primitive. Regenerated token estimate is simpler but depends on model instrumentation.
- Billing audits: customers may want proofs. We'll need to surface a per-request sample log (hashed) showing regenerated_tokens/gpu_ms and cache-hit tags.

Gaming / incentives
----
Be careful: customers might try to craft prompts to maximize cache reuse to get discounts while preserving user-visible work (valid for some apps, but could be gaming). Consider rate limits on cache-credit eligible requests or minimum thresholds.

Ops and implementability notes
----
- Runtime: add a per-request metric: {regenerated_tokens_estimate:int, cache_hit_fraction:float, cache_source: enum}
- Billing pipeline: aggregate regenerated_tokens by customer per billing period, apply per-regened-token rate and baseline per-request fees.
- Console: show moving avg cache-hit and estimated monthly savings vs naive per-token model (marketing angle!).
- Migration: default to legacy per-token billing for first 3 months while we run cache-aware in "reporting only" to debug.

Open questions / TODOs
----
- Get real telemetry for avg_gpu_ms_per_token across models (request to infra/team). (Assigned: Aisha)
- Estimate noise and variance in regenerated_tokens_estimate; what threshold do we need for stable invoices?
- Decide baseline per-request fee (cover routing/IO). Current guess $0.00025 – $0.001 per req. Need finance check.
- Product language: what to call this on invoice? "Cache-aware tokens" vs "compute tokens" vs "regenerated tokens". "Compute tokens" might be friendlier.
- Legal: T&Cs and audit logs; confirm with finance and legal on evidence for credits.

Quick actionable next steps (for next week)
----
1) Ask infra/telemetry for sample distribution: per-customer cache_hit_fraction, regenerated_tokens_estimate, and mean gpu-ms by model for November-February. (Noah)
2) Run a simulator to map how much revenue delta we expect across top 50 customers under a conservative per-regened-token price. (Aisha)
3) Draft short internal explainer (one-pager) for sales/CS with example invoices and Q&A. (Lina)

Notes to self
----
- Keep the billing primitive simple — customers hate surprises. Prefer small baseline + regen-token price.
- Be explicit in console about the difference between "tokens billed" vs "user-visible tokens".
- This could be a competitive angle vs vendors that only bill per output token (we can market that we pass-through cache savings).

End of scratchpad.
